history.q: In 1896, Ethiopian forces decisively defeated which European army at the Battle of Adwa?
history.fact: Victory at Adwa on 1 March 1896 secured Ethiopia's independence, and the day is still celebrated as a national holiday.

history.q: Which emperor ruled Ethiopia from his coronation in 1930 until he was deposed in 1974?
history.fact: He had served as regent since 1916, and his November 1930 coronation in Addis Ababa drew dignitaries from around the world.

history.q: What nickname was given to the 3.2-million-year-old hominin skeleton found in Ethiopia's Afar region in 1974?
history.fact: She was named after the Beatles song 'Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds'; in Ethiopia she is known as Dinkinesh, 'you are marvellous'.

history.q: Which ruler, later emperor, founded Addis Ababa in 1886 with his wife Taytu?
history.fact: Taytu is said to have chosen the site near hot springs; Addis Ababa means 'new flower' in Amharic.

history.q: Which ancient kingdom, famous for its towering carved stone stelae, was centred in northern Ethiopia?
history.fact: Aksum traded across the Red Sea with Rome and India and minted its own gold, silver and bronze coins.

history.q: Ethiopia's Solomonic dynasty traced its descent to King Solomon and which legendary queen?
history.fact: Ethiopian tradition holds that Makeda, Queen of Sheba, bore Solomon a son, Menelik I, founder of the royal line.

history.q: Apart from Ethiopia, which African country avoided European colonisation during the Scramble for Africa?
history.fact: Ethiopia's green, yellow and red flag inspired the colours adopted by many newly independent African nations.

history.q: To which international body did Haile Selassie make a famous appeal in Geneva in 1936 after Italy's invasion?
history.fact: He warned the assembly that 'it is us today; it will be you tomorrow'. The League's weak response damaged its credibility.

history.q: A devastating famine in Ethiopia in 1984-85 inspired which famous 1985 charity concerts?
history.fact: Live Aid followed Band Aid's 1984 single 'Do They Know It's Christmas?' and was broadcast from London and Philadelphia.

history.q: Which 4th-century Aksumite king made Christianity the kingdom's official religion?
history.fact: Ezana's coins are among the earliest in the world to bear the Christian cross.

history.q: What was the name of the military committee that deposed Emperor Haile Selassie in 1974?
history.fact: 'Derg' means 'committee' or 'council' in the ancient Ge'ez language.

history.q: Which emperor took his own life at Magdala in 1868 rather than surrender to a British expedition?
history.fact: Tewodros had imprisoned British envoys; Napier's troops later carried off hundreds of manuscripts and treasures from Magdala.

history.q: Which city did Emperor Fasilides make his capital in the 1630s, building a royal castle compound?
history.fact: The castles of Fasil Ghebbi blend Ethiopian, Portuguese and Indian influences and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

history.q: Disputed translations of which 1889 treaty led to the First Italo-Ethiopian War?
history.fact: Italy claimed the treaty made Ethiopia its protectorate, but the Amharic version contained no such obligation.

history.q: Alongside Ethiopian resistance fighters, troops of which country helped restore Haile Selassie to power in 1941?
history.fact: The emperor re-entered Addis Ababa on 5 May 1941, five years to the day after Italian troops had occupied it.

history.q: Which empress, daughter of Menelik II, reigned from 1916 to 1930 with Ras Tafari as her regent?
history.fact: On Zewditu's death in 1930, Ras Tafari succeeded her and was crowned Emperor Haile Selassie.

history.q: Which European nation sent soldiers led by Cristóvão da Gama to aid Ethiopia's emperor in 1541?
history.fact: Da Gama, a son of explorer Vasco da Gama, was killed in 1542, but the allied army won decisively the following year.

history.q: Haile Selassie is revered as a messianic figure by which religious movement that arose in Jamaica?
history.fact: The movement takes its name from Ras Tafari, the emperor's title before his 1930 coronation.

history.q: What name is given to the 1769-1855 period when regional lords held real power and emperors were figureheads?
history.fact: Known in Amharic as Zemene Mesafint, the era ended when Kassa Hailu was crowned Emperor Tewodros II in 1855.

history.q: Which 6th-century Aksumite king led an expedition across the Red Sea to the kingdom of Himyar in Yemen?
history.fact: Kaleb's campaign briefly brought southern Arabia under Aksumite influence; he is venerated as a saint.

history.q: Which ruler founded the Solomonic dynasty in 1270, ending the rule of the Zagwe kings?
history.fact: The dynasty he founded would rule, with interruptions, until Haile Selassie was deposed in 1974.

history.q: At which 1543 battle near Lake Tana was Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi killed?
history.fact: His death ended a campaign that had swept across the Ethiopian highlands for over a decade.

history.q: Emperor Yohannes IV was killed in 1889 at the Battle of Metemma fighting the forces of which state?
history.fact: Yohannes was mortally wounded just as his army appeared to be winning; his death opened the way for Menelik II.

history.q: What was Emperor Tewodros II's name before he was crowned in 1855?
history.fact: Tewodros dreamed of modernising Ethiopia and even had European missionaries cast a giant mortar he named Sevastopol.

history.q: Which Portuguese priest wrote one of the first European eyewitness accounts of Lalibela's churches in the 1520s?
history.fact: Álvares wrote that he feared readers would not believe his descriptions of the rock-hewn churches.

technology.q: According to Ethiopian legend, how did the goatherd Kaldi discover coffee?
choices: His goats fell asleep under a coffee tree
His goats became lively after eating the berries
Coffee berries turned his goats' milk brown
A monk roasted beans he found in a cave
technology.fact: One version says local monks then brewed the berries into a drink to stay awake during long night prayers.

technology.q: Ethiopia is Africa's largest producer of which crop?
technology.fact: Wild Coffea arabica still grows in the highland forests of south-western Ethiopia, the species' original home.

technology.q: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam was built on which river?
technology.fact: With a planned capacity of over 5,000 megawatts, it is Africa's largest hydroelectric project.

technology.q: Which state-owned carrier, founded in 1945, has grown into Africa's largest airline group?
technology.fact: Ethiopian Airlines' first international flight in 1946 went from Addis Ababa to Cairo using a Douglas C-47.

technology.q: The electrified standard-gauge railway that opened in the late 2010s links Addis Ababa to a port in which country?
technology.fact: Landlocked since 1993, Ethiopia sends most of its foreign trade through the port of Djibouti.

technology.q: How many months are there in Ethiopia's traditional calendar?
technology.fact: Twelve 30-day months are followed by a short month of five or six days, hence the slogan '13 months of sunshine'.

technology.q: Which source generates the vast majority of Ethiopia's electricity?
technology.fact: Rivers tumbling off the Ethiopian Highlands give the country one of the largest hydropower potentials in Africa.

technology.q: For centuries, camel caravans have carried slabs of which commodity out of the Danakil Depression?
technology.fact: Rectangular salt bars called amole were once used as currency across the Ethiopian Highlands.

technology.q: Fossil sites in Ethiopia's Afar region are especially important to scientists studying what?
technology.fact: The Middle Awash valley alone has yielded fossils of human ancestors spanning roughly six million years.

technology.q: Which American paleoanthropologist co-led the team that found the 'Lucy' skeleton in 1974?
technology.fact: Johanson and his student Tom Gray spotted a fragment of arm bone in a gully at Hadar on 24 November 1974.

technology.q: The 'Lucy' skeleton belongs to which species of early human ancestor?
technology.fact: The species is named after the Afar region; Lucy walked upright but stood only about 1.1 metres tall.

technology.q: Ethiopia's first satellite, ETRSS-1, was launched in December 2019 from which country?
technology.fact: The small Earth-observation satellite was designed to monitor crops, weather and the environment.

technology.q: Ethiopian Airlines' main hub is which airport?
technology.fact: Bole sits at about 2,300 metres above sea level, one of the highest major international hubs in the world.

technology.q: In 2012, Ethiopian Airlines became the first African airline to receive which new airliner?
technology.fact: The carbon-composite 787 suited Ethiopian's high-altitude hub, where thin air demands efficient long-haul jets.

technology.q: The Addis Ababa Light Rail, opened in 2015, was largely financed and built with help from which country?
technology.fact: It was hailed as the first modern light rail system in sub-Saharan Africa.

technology.q: Ethiopia has become one of Africa's leading exporters of which horticultural product, especially to Europe?
technology.fact: Roses grown in greenhouses around Addis Ababa are flown overnight to flower auctions in the Netherlands.

technology.q: The Hawassa Industrial Park, inaugurated in 2016, focuses on which industry?
technology.fact: It was promoted as an eco-industrial park powered by hydroelectricity, with zero liquid discharge of wastewater.

technology.q: Ethiopian-born scientist Gebisa Ejeta won the 2009 World Food Prize for drought-resistant hybrids of which crop?
technology.fact: His hybrids also resisted Striga, a parasitic weed that devastates cereal crops across Africa.

technology.q: Ethiopian scientist Aklilu Lemma found that the endod soapberry kills snails that spread which disease?
technology.fact: He noticed dead snails downstream from where people washed clothes with endod berries; he won a Right Livelihood Award in 1989.

technology.q: Some of the oldest known Oldowan stone tools, about 2.6 million years old, were found at which Ethiopian site?
technology.fact: The Gona finds pushed back the known start of systematic stone-tool making by hundreds of thousands of years.

technology.q: The 4.4-million-year-old fossil skeleton 'Ardi', described in 2009, belongs to which genus?
technology.fact: Ardi had a grasping big toe for climbing trees yet could also walk upright on the ground.

technology.q: Which Ethiopian paleoanthropologist discovered the fossil child 'Selam' at Dikika?
technology.fact: Selam, about 3.3 million years old, is often called 'Lucy's baby', though she lived about 100,000 years before Lucy.

technology.q: Since 2008, Ethiopia's Wollo region has become famous for which gemstones?
technology.fact: Welo opals often show vivid play-of-colour and are mined by hand from cliffs in the northern highlands.

technology.q: The Gilgel Gibe III hydroelectric dam, completed in the mid-2010s, stands on which river?
technology.fact: The Omo flows south from the dam into Lake Turkana, which lies mostly in Kenya.

technology.q: The original metre-gauge railway from Djibouti, completed to Addis Ababa in 1917, was built by a company from which country?
technology.fact: The 'Chemin de fer franco-éthiopien' took about two decades to build and ran for roughly a century.

art.q: How were the famous medieval churches of Lalibela created?
art.fact: Each church was hewn from the living volcanic rock, so the builders worked downwards, removing stone rather than adding it.

art.q: Seen from above, Lalibela's Church of St George (Bete Giyorgis) is carved in what shape?
art.fact: Bete Giyorgis sits about 12 metres down in a pit and is reached through a trench and tunnel cut into the rock.

art.q: Which country returned the looted Obelisk of Aksum to Ethiopia in 2005?
art.fact: Taken to Rome in 1937, the 24-metre stele was flown home in three pieces and re-erected in Aksum in 2008.

art.q: Eskista, Ethiopia's famous traditional dance, is known for rapid movements of which part of the body?
art.fact: Dancers bounce, roll and shake their shoulders at dazzling speed while keeping the rest of the body almost still.

art.q: King Lalibela is said to have built his rock churches as a 'New' version of which holy city?
art.fact: The site even has a stream named the Yordanos, after the River Jordan.

art.q: The giant stelae of Aksum are carved to resemble what?
art.fact: False doors, windows and beam-ends are carved into the granite, mimicking Aksumite palaces many storeys high.

art.q: The krar, a popular Ethiopian instrument, belongs to which family of instruments?
art.fact: The five- or six-stringed krar is played by plucking or strumming and often accompanies singers at celebrations.

art.q: Which musician is known as the father of Ethio-jazz?
art.fact: Mulatu studied in London and Boston; his music featured in Jim Jarmusch's 2005 film 'Broken Flowers'.

art.q: Ethiopian-born Haile Gerima is acclaimed for his work in which art form?
art.fact: His 1993 film 'Sankofa', about slavery in the Americas, became an independent hit in the United States.

art.q: How many medieval monolithic churches make up the Lalibela complex?
art.fact: The churches were carved in the late 12th and early 13th centuries and became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978.

art.q: King Lalibela, who gave his name to the rock churches, belonged to which dynasty?
art.fact: The Zagwe kings ruled from their capital at Roha, which was later renamed Lalibela in the king's honour.

art.q: Gondar's Debre Berhan Selassie church is famous for a ceiling painted with what?
art.fact: Legend says a swarm of bees drove away raiders who attacked Gondar in 1888, saving the church.

art.q: Which 14th-century Ge'ez text tells the story of the Queen of Sheba, King Solomon and their son Menelik I?
art.fact: Its title means 'Glory of the Kings', and it served for centuries as a founding epic of Ethiopia's monarchy.

art.q: Maaza Mengiste's novel 'The Shadow King', shortlisted for the 2020 Booker Prize, is set during which conflict?
art.fact: The novel highlights women who fought against the Italian invasion.

art.q: 'Tizita', both a musical mode and a much-loved song genre in Ethiopia, expresses what feeling?
art.fact: Tizita is often compared to the blues or Portuguese saudade; almost every major Ethiopian singer has recorded one.

art.q: Which popular Ethiopian singer was born Tewodros Kassahun?
art.fact: Many of his songs draw on Ethiopian history; the title track of his 2012 album 'Tikur Sew' honours Menelik II and the victory at Adwa.

art.q: The masenqo, played by Ethiopian minstrels called azmari, is what kind of instrument?
art.fact: Azmaris improvise witty, often teasing verses about their audience while playing in bars and at weddings.

art.q: In traditional Ethiopian church painting, how are holy figures usually shown, in contrast to evil ones?
art.fact: Villains and demons are typically painted in profile, showing only one eye.

art.q: Painter Afewerk Tekle created the huge stained-glass windows of which Addis Ababa building, home of the UN Economic Commission for Africa?
art.fact: The triptych of windows, unveiled in the early 1960s, depicts Africa's past suffering, present struggle and hoped-for future.

art.q: The Garima Gospels, kept in an Ethiopian monastery, are famous for being what?
choices: The first book printed in Africa
Among the oldest illustrated Christian manuscripts
art.fact: Radiocarbon dating suggests they were made between roughly 330 and 650 CE.

art.q: What is thought to have happened to the Great Stele of Aksum, about 33 metres long?
choices: It was buried by a volcanic eruption
It was cut up to build a church
It collapsed during or soon after being raised
art.fact: Weighing around 500 tonnes, it may be the largest single block of stone humans ever tried to stand upright.

art.q: Haile Gerima's film 'Teza' won the Special Jury Prize at which 2008 film festival?
art.fact: 'Teza', meaning 'morning dew', also won the top prize, the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, at Burkina Faso's FESPACO in 2009.

art.q: Who wrote 'Fikir Eske Mekabir' ('Love unto the Grave'), often called the greatest Amharic novel?
art.fact: Published in the 1960s, the novel's love story is set against the rigid class system of rural Gojjam.

art.q: Yared Zeleke's 'Lamb' (2015) was the first Ethiopian film chosen for the official selection of which festival?
art.fact: The film follows a boy who tries to save his beloved sheep from being sacrificed for a feast.

art.q: Addis Ababa-born artist Julie Mehretu is best known for what kind of work?
art.fact: Her vast canvases layer architectural drawings, maps and gestural marks; she received a MacArthur 'genius' grant in 2005.

politics.q: Which pan-African organisation has its headquarters in Addis Ababa?
politics.fact: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002; its headquarters complex in Addis Ababa opened in 2012.

politics.q: Who became prime minister of Ethiopia in April 2018?
politics.fact: Abiy Ahmed took office on 2 April 2018, chosen by the then-ruling coalition after his predecessor resigned.

politics.q: Under its 1995 constitution, what type of state is Ethiopia?
politics.fact: The constitution renamed the country the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, made up of regional states and chartered cities.

politics.q: Which country formally became independent from Ethiopia in 1993 after a referendum?
politics.fact: Eritreans voted overwhelmingly for independence in April 1993, leaving Ethiopia without a coastline.

politics.q: In Ethiopia's parliamentary system, who holds most executive power?
politics.fact: The president, elected by parliament for a six-year term, plays a largely ceremonial role.

politics.q: In 1945, Ethiopia was among the founding members of which organisation?
politics.fact: Ethiopia was one of the 51 original member states that signed the UN Charter, having been a victim of aggression in the 1930s.

politics.q: In 2018, Sahle-Work Zewde became Ethiopia's first woman to hold which office?
politics.fact: A veteran diplomat, she had previously headed the United Nations Office at Nairobi.

politics.q: What did the Ethiopian imperial title 'Negusa Nagast' mean?
politics.fact: Emperors used the title to signal their authority over regional kings and nobles across the empire.

politics.q: Which emperor gave Ethiopia its first written constitution in 1931?
politics.fact: The 1931 constitution created a two-chamber parliament, though its members were appointed or chosen by the nobility.

politics.q: Which organisation was founded in Addis Ababa on 25 May 1963?
politics.fact: The founding date is still celebrated across the continent as Africa Day.

politics.q: Who led Ethiopia's Derg military government from 1977 until 1991?
politics.fact: Mengistu also served as president of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia from 1987.

politics.q: Who served as Ethiopia's prime minister from 1995 until his death in 2012?
politics.fact: Meles had led the transitional government from 1991 before becoming prime minister under the new constitution.

politics.q: Who succeeded Meles Zenawi as Ethiopia's prime minister in 2012?
politics.fact: Hailemariam, previously deputy prime minister and foreign minister, served until he announced his resignation in February 2018.

politics.q: What is the name of the lower, directly elected house of Ethiopia's parliament?
politics.fact: Its members serve five-year terms, and the house elects the prime minister from among its ranks.

politics.q: Under a 1950 UN resolution, how was Eritrea joined to Ethiopia in 1952?
choices: As an autonomous unit in a federation
politics.fact: Haile Selassie dissolved the federation in 1962, making Eritrea a province of Ethiopia.

politics.q: Besides Addis Ababa, which Ethiopian city is administered as a chartered city rather than within a regional state?
politics.fact: Dire Dawa grew up around a station on the railway from Djibouti in the early 20th century.

politics.q: After his government fell in 1991, Mengistu Haile Mariam went into exile in which country?
politics.fact: He fled in May 1991 as rebel forces closed in on Addis Ababa and settled in Harare.

politics.q: Ethiopia's Kagnew Battalions fought under the United Nations Command in which war?
politics.fact: Haile Selassie sent the battalions in rotation from 1951; Ethiopia and South Africa were the only African nations to send forces.

politics.q: Which chamber of Ethiopia's parliament has the power to interpret the constitution?
politics.fact: Rather than a constitutional court, Ethiopia gives this role to the upper house, advised by a council of legal experts.

politics.q: In which year was Ethiopia admitted to the League of Nations?
politics.fact: As a condition of membership, Ethiopia pledged to work towards abolishing slavery.

politics.q: Who became Ethiopia's first president under the 1995 constitution?
politics.fact: Negasso served from 1995 to 2001 and later became an independent member of parliament.

politics.q: Who served as Ethiopia's president from 2001 to 2013?
politics.fact: He had first sat in parliament during Haile Selassie's reign, decades before becoming head of state.

politics.q: An attempted coup against Haile Selassie in December 1960 took place while he was visiting which country?
politics.fact: Loyal army units crushed the attempt within days, and the emperor returned to Addis Ababa.

politics.q: Which grandson of Menelik II ruled as uncrowned emperor until he was deposed in 1916?
politics.fact: Lij Iyasu was designated heir in 1909 but never crowned; Zewditu became empress after his removal.

politics.q: In which year did Haile Selassie proclaim a revised constitution that introduced an elected lower chamber?
politics.fact: The first elections for the Chamber of Deputies under universal adult suffrage followed in 1957.

current-affairs.q: Which Ethiopian leader was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in October 2019?
current-affairs.fact: The Nobel Committee cited in particular his initiative to resolve the long border dispute with neighbouring Eritrea.

current-affairs.q: Which major project did Ethiopia officially inaugurate in September 2025?
current-affairs.fact: Built on the Blue Nile near the border with Sudan, the dam has a planned capacity of over 5,000 megawatts.

current-affairs.q: In July 2019, Ethiopia reported that volunteers had planted roughly how many tree seedlings in a single day?
current-affairs.fact: The mass planting was part of the national Green Legacy Initiative to restore forests and fight land degradation.

current-affairs.q: Which group of major emerging economies did Ethiopia join as a full member on 1 January 2024?
current-affairs.fact: Ethiopia joined alongside Egypt, Iran and the United Arab Emirates in the bloc's first big expansion since South Africa joined in 2010.

current-affairs.q: Which Ethiopian runner won the men's marathon at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
current-affairs.fact: A late call-up to the team, he won in an Olympic record of 2:06:26.

current-affairs.q: In July 2024, Ethiopia's central bank let which currency's exchange rate be set by the market?
current-affairs.fact: The move ended years of a tightly controlled official exchange rate, as part of a wider economic reform programme.

current-affairs.q: The March 2019 crash of Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 led to the worldwide grounding of which aircraft model?
current-affairs.fact: Regulators around the world grounded the type for about 20 months while its flight-control software was redesigned.

current-affairs.q: Which city hosted the second Africa Climate Summit in September 2025?
current-affairs.fact: The first Africa Climate Summit had been held in Nairobi, Kenya, in September 2023.

current-affairs.q: In early 2024, Ethiopia announced a ban on importing which kind of private car?
current-affairs.fact: Ethiopia, which generates most of its power from hydroelectric dams, aims to cut costly fuel imports.

current-affairs.q: Who was elected president of Ethiopia by parliament in October 2024?
current-affairs.fact: A career diplomat, he had previously served as Ethiopia's ambassador to the UN and as foreign minister.

current-affairs.q: Which party won Ethiopia's general election held in June 2021?
current-affairs.fact: The party had been formed in December 2019 by merging most members of the former ruling EPRDF coalition.

current-affairs.q: In which city did Tigst Assefa set a women's marathon world record in September 2023?
current-affairs.fact: She ran 2:11:53, taking more than two minutes off the previous record.

current-affairs.q: Which Ethiopian won the men's 10,000 m at the Tokyo Olympics, held in 2021?
current-affairs.fact: Barega outsprinted Uganda's Joshua Cheptegei to claim Ethiopia's first gold of the Games.

current-affairs.q: In October 2022, which company launched mobile services in Ethiopia, ending Ethio Telecom's monopoly?
current-affairs.fact: The Kenyan operator led an international consortium that won Ethiopia's first private telecom licence in 2021.

current-affairs.q: What is the name of the mobile money service Ethio Telecom launched in May 2021?
current-affairs.fact: The name combines 'tele' with the birr, Ethiopia's currency; it gained millions of users within its first year.

current-affairs.q: What did Ethiopia launch in Addis Ababa in January 2025?
current-affairs.fact: It was Ethiopia's first stock exchange in about five decades, after an earlier share market was closed in the 1970s.

current-affairs.q: Unity Park, opened in Addis Ababa in October 2019, lies in the grounds of which historic site?
current-affairs.fact: Visitors can tour former royal halls and banqueting rooms, as well as gardens and a zoo.

current-affairs.q: In August 2025, the original 'Lucy' fossil went on display outside Ethiopia in which European capital?
current-affairs.fact: It was Lucy's first trip abroad since a six-year tour of the United States ended in 2013.

current-affairs.q: In October 2021, Letesenbet Gidey became the first woman to run a half marathon in under how long?
current-affairs.fact: She clocked 1:02:52 in Valencia, a city where she had also set a 5,000 m world record the year before.

current-affairs.q: Which Ethiopian broke the men's half marathon world record in Valencia in October 2024?
current-affairs.fact: His 57:30 took one second off Jacob Kiplimo's record; Kiplimo lowered it again in early 2025.

current-affairs.q: In 2023, which Ethiopian national park was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List?
current-affairs.fact: The park's high Sanetti Plateau is home to the largest population of the endangered Ethiopian wolf.

current-affairs.q: At which distance did Gudaf Tsegay set a world record in Eugene in September 2023?
current-affairs.fact: Her 14:00.21 cut about five seconds off the record Kenya's Faith Kipyegon had set just three months earlier.

current-affairs.q: Who won the women's marathon at the 2022 World Athletics Championships in Eugene?
current-affairs.fact: Her winning time of 2:18:11 set a new championship record.

current-affairs.q: In which year did the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam first generate electricity?
current-affairs.fact: The first turbine was switched on in February 2022, more than a decade after construction began in 2011.

current-affairs.q: In June 2023, Lamecha Girma set a world record in which event at a meeting in Paris?
current-affairs.fact: His 7:52.11 broke a steeplechase record that had stood since 2004.

society.q: During 2022, Ethiopia's annual inflation rate hovered around what level?
society.fact: Food prices rose fastest, with inflation above 30% for much of 2022 and 2023 before easing in 2024.

society.q: Which product was Ethiopia's biggest export earner throughout the early 2020s?
society.fact: Ethiopia is Africa's largest coffee producer, and millions of smallholder households depend on the crop for cash income.

society.q: In 2023, the median age of Ethiopia's population was roughly what?
society.fact: Roughly 40% of Ethiopians were under 15, making job creation for young people a central economic issue.

society.q: In 2022, UN estimates put Ethiopia's population at roughly how many people?
society.fact: The country adds over 2.5 million people a year and is projected to pass 200 million by around 2050.

society.q: Between 2020 and 2023, southern and eastern Ethiopia endured the Horn of Africa's worst drought in roughly how many years?
society.fact: Five consecutive rainy seasons failed, devastating pastoralist herds in the Somali and Oromia regions.

society.q: In the early 2020s, which sector still employed the majority of Ethiopia's workforce?
society.fact: Around two-thirds of workers were in farming, mostly on small rain-fed plots, so harvests shape the whole economy.

society.q: According to World Bank data for 2022, roughly what share of Ethiopians had access to electricity?
society.fact: Access is far higher in cities than in the countryside, where many households still rely on kerosene and firewood.

society.q: In July 2022, Ethiopia began phasing out subsidies on what, sending prices sharply higher?
society.fact: Public transport operators were initially exempted to soften the blow for commuters in Addis Ababa.

society.q: In 2023, Ethiopia's government said a large irrigation drive meant it would stop importing which staple grain?
society.fact: Lowland irrigated wheat was planted on hundreds of thousands of hectares; analysts questioned how much was actually exported.

society.q: In December 2023, Ethiopia became the third African country in three years to default on what?
society.fact: It missed a $33m coupon on its only international bond, following Zambia and Ghana into default.

society.q: By 2024, Ethiopia was hosting roughly how many refugees, one of the largest numbers in Africa?
society.fact: Most came from South Sudan, Somalia, Eritrea and Sudan, and were housed in camps near the borders.

society.q: In October 2018, Ethiopia formed a cabinet in which what share of ministers were women?
society.fact: Ten of the twenty ministers were women, including the heads of defence and peace, a first for Ethiopia.

society.q: As of 2024, Ethiopia was unusual among large countries in lacking what for private-sector workers?
society.fact: A 2019 labour law allowed for a wage board to set one, but no national minimum wage had been fixed.

society.q: When Ethiopia replaced its banknotes in September 2020, how long were people given to swap old notes?
society.fact: A new 200-birr note was introduced, and cash withdrawals were capped to push hoarded money back into banks.

society.q: In October 2024, Ethiopia offered the public shares in which state company for the first time?
society.fact: Ten percent of the company was offered at 300 birr a share, with purchases made through the telebirr app.

society.q: In which year did Ethiopia last hold a national population census?
society.fact: A fourth census has been postponed repeatedly since 2017, so population figures rely on projections.

society.q: By the end of 2024, a few months after the birr was floated, one US dollar bought roughly how many birr at banks?
society.fact: The rate had been held near 57 birr before the July 2024 reform, so imported goods became much dearer.

society.q: In the 2022 national school-leaving exam, roughly what share of Ethiopian students scored the 50% needed for university?
society.fact: Only about 30,000 of nearly 900,000 candidates passed after exams were moved to university campuses to curb cheating.

society.q: In July 2024, alongside the currency float, the IMF approved a four-year programme for Ethiopia worth roughly how much?
society.fact: About $1bn was released immediately, and the deal unlocked further World Bank financing for the reforms.

society.q: Ethiopia's Productive Safety Net Programme, which gives cash or food for work, supported roughly how many people in 2020?
society.fact: Launched in 2005, it is one of Africa's largest social protection schemes and is backed by the World Bank.

society.q: What is 'Fayda', rolled out in Ethiopia from 2021?
society.fact: The biometric ID is being linked to banking and other public services; the original target of 90 million registrations by 2025 was later pushed back to 2028.

society.q: What is the name of the scheme launched in 2024 that widened roads and cleared old neighbourhoods across Addis Ababa?
society.fact: It added cycle lanes and pavements but displaced many residents and traders from inner-city areas.

society.q: Ethiopia's 2021 labour force survey put urban unemployment at roughly what rate?
society.fact: Rural unemployment was only about 5%, but much rural work is unpaid or seasonal on family farms.

society.q: In early 2021, Ethiopia became one of the first countries to seek debt relief under which G20 initiative?
society.fact: Talks with creditors dragged on for years, and a bilateral debt restructuring deal was only agreed in 2025.

society.q: In 2024, Ethiopia's central bank introduced its first formal policy interest rate, set at what level?
society.fact: The move was part of a shift from directly rationing credit towards steering the economy with interest rates.

general.q: What is the capital of Ethiopia?
general.fact: At about 2,350 metres above sea level, Addis Ababa is one of the highest capital cities in the world.

general.q: Injera, Ethiopia's spongy sourdough flatbread, is traditionally made from which grain?
general.fact: Teff is one of the world's smallest grains and is naturally gluten-free; injera doubles as plate and cutlery.

general.q: Which Ethiopian lake is the source of the Blue Nile?
general.fact: Lake Tana, Ethiopia's largest lake, is dotted with islands holding centuries-old monasteries.

general.q: Which Ethiopian runner won Olympic 10,000 m gold in both 1996 and 2000?
general.fact: Haile also set a marathon world record of 2:03:59 in Berlin in 2008.

general.q: Abebe Bikila famously won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome how?
choices: Running backwards for the last mile
After stopping to help a rival
general.fact: He won again in Tokyo in 1964, this time wearing shoes, becoming the first person to retain the Olympic marathon title.

general.q: Ethiopia is Africa's second most populous country after which nation?
general.fact: Ethiopia is also the world's most populous landlocked country.

general.q: Berbere, essential to Ethiopian cooking, is what?
general.fact: Berbere typically combines dried chillies with spices such as fenugreek, coriander and cardamom; it gives wat stews their deep red colour.

general.q: Ethiopia's high central plateau is often nicknamed the 'Roof of' what?
general.fact: The highlands rise above 4,000 metres in places and feed the Blue Nile and many other rivers.

general.q: Which walled city in eastern Ethiopia is famous for its 'hyena men', who feed wild hyenas at night?
general.fact: The hyena men call the animals by name and sometimes feed them meat from a stick held in their mouths.

general.q: Amharic is written in which script?
general.fact: The Ge'ez script is an abugida: each character stands for a consonant combined with a vowel.

general.q: Which hydrothermal field in the Danakil Depression is famous for its yellow, green and orange mineral pools?
general.fact: Dallol has recorded one of the highest average annual temperatures of any inhabited place on Earth.

general.q: In the traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony, coffee is brewed in a long-necked clay pot called what?
general.fact: Guests traditionally drink three rounds, called abol, tona and baraka.

general.q: Enkutatash, the Ethiopian New Year, falls in which Gregorian month?
general.fact: It usually falls on 11 September, at the end of the rainy season, when yellow meskel daisies bloom.

general.q: What is the highest mountain in Ethiopia?
general.fact: Rising to about 4,550 metres in the Simien Mountains, it is one of Africa's highest peaks.

general.q: Which grass-eating primate, found only in the Ethiopian Highlands, has a bright red patch on its chest?
general.fact: Geladas spend nights on cliff ledges and gather in herds of hundreds to graze on the high plateaus.

general.q: Which Ethiopian became the first Black African woman to win Olympic gold, in the 10,000 m in 1992?
general.fact: After her Barcelona win, she ran a victory lap hand in hand with South Africa's Elana Meyer, who took silver.

general.q: In 1962, Ethiopia won which football tournament on home soil?
general.fact: Ethiopia beat the United Arab Republic (Egypt) 4-2 after extra time in the final in Addis Ababa.

general.q: In traditional Ethiopian timekeeping, when does the 12-hour daytime count begin?
general.fact: So '1 o'clock' in Ethiopian time is 7 a.m., a common source of confusion for visitors making appointments.

general.q: Doro wat, a festive Ethiopian stew, is made with which main ingredient?
general.fact: It is slow-cooked with onions, berbere and spiced butter and usually served with hard-boiled eggs.

general.q: What is the local name for the Blue Nile Falls, meaning 'great smoke'?
general.fact: The falls' flow has been greatly reduced since a hydroelectric station was built upstream.

general.q: Sof Omar, in south-eastern Ethiopia, is one of Africa's longest what?
general.fact: The Weyib River carved its passages, pillars and domed chambers through limestone.

general.q: Which Ethiopian, nicknamed 'Yifter the Shifter', won the 5,000 m and 10,000 m at the 1980 Moscow Olympics?
general.fact: His nickname came from his devastating change of pace on the final lap.

general.q: Which Ethiopian runner won the Olympic marathon at Mexico City in 1968?
general.fact: Mamo also took silver in the 10,000 m at the same Games.

general.q: What is 'gursha' in Ethiopian dining culture?
choices: A toast made with honey wine
Hand-feeding a mouthful to a companion
general.fact: The bigger the gursha you offer, the stronger the bond of friendship or affection it shows.

general.q: Which wild goat is found only in Ethiopia's Simien Mountains?
general.fact: Ethiopia's national football team is nicknamed the Walias after this rare, cliff-climbing goat.
